data.title: What is Data?
data.intro: Data is information we collect about something.
data.example1: How many pets each student has
data.example2: Favorite ice cream flavors in your class
data.example4: Number of books read each month

graphs.title: What are Graphs?
graphs.intro: Graphs are visual ways to show data.
graphs.purpose: They help us see patterns and compare information quickly.

barGraphs.title: 1. Bar Graphs
barGraphs.explanation: Bar graphs use rectangular bars to show amounts. The height (or length) of each bar shows how much of something there is.

pictographs.title: 2. Pictographs
pictographs.explanation: Pictographs use pictures or symbols to represent data. Each picture stands for a certain number of items.

linePlots.title: 3. Line Plots
linePlots.explanation: Line plots show data as marks (usually X's) above a number line. They're great for showing how often different numbers appear.

tables.title: 4. Data Tables
tables.explanation: Data tables organize information in rows and columns, making it easy to read and compare.

barGraph.title: Example: Bar Graph
barGraph.caption: This bar graph shows how many students chose each fruit as their favorite.

pictograph.title: Example: Pictograph
pictograph.caption: Each symbol represents 2 pieces of fruit sold.

linePlot.title: Example: Line Plot
linePlot.caption: Each X shows one student. The number shows how many books they read.

dataTable.title: Example: Data Table
dataTable.caption: This table shows student scores on a test.

readingBarGraphs.title: How to Read a Bar Graph:
readingBarGraphs.step1: Look at the title to understand what data is shown
readingBarGraphs.step2: Check the labels on both axes
readingBarGraphs.step3: Find the bar you're interested in
readingBarGraphs.step4: Look at where the top of the bar reaches on the scale

readingPictographs.title: How to Read a Pictograph:
readingPictographs.step1: Check the key to see what each symbol represents
readingPictographs.step2: Count the number of symbols in a row
readingPictographs.step3: Multiply by the value of each symbol

example1.title: Reading a Bar Graph
example1.question: Looking at our Favorite Fruits bar graph, which fruit was chosen by the most students?
example1.step1: Look at all the bars and compare their heights
example1.step3: The top of the Orange bar reaches 8 on the scale
example1.step4: This means 8 students chose Orange as their favorite
example1.answer: Orange was chosen by the most students (8 students).

example2.title: Reading a Pictograph
example2.question: In our Fruit Sales pictograph, how many apples were sold?

example3.title: Reading a Line Plot
example3.question: In our Books Read line plot, how many students read exactly 4 books?
example3.step1: Find the number 4 on the number line
example3.step3: There are 4 X marks above the number 4

exercise1.question: Look at the Favorite Fruits bar graph. How many students chose Banana?
exercise1.explanation: The Banana bar reaches up to 4 on the scale, so 4 students chose Banana.

exercise2.question: In the Fruit Sales pictograph, how many oranges were sold? (Remember: each symbol = 2 fruits)
exercise2.hint: Count the orange symbols and multiply by 2.
exercise2.explanation: There are 5 orange symbols, and each represents 2 fruits: 5 × 2 = 10 oranges.

exercise3.question: Looking at the Books Read line plot, what is the most common number of books read?
exercise3.explanation: The number 4 has the most X marks (4 marks), so 4 books is the most common.

exercise4.question: In the Books Read line plot, how many students read 2 books?
exercise4.hint: Count the X marks above the number 2.
exercise4.explanation: There are 3 X marks above the number 2, so 3 students read 2 books.

exercise5.question: In the student scores table, who scored the highest on the test?
exercise5.explanation: Looking at all the scores in the table, Alice has the highest score of 95.

notes.title: Tips & Tricks
notes.tip1: 📊 Always read the title and labels first! They tell you what the graph is showing.
notes.tip2: 🔍 In pictographs, always check the key to know what each symbol represents.
notes.trick1: 💡 To find the total in a bar graph, add up all the bar values.
notes.warning1: ⚠️ Make sure you're reading the correct axis (horizontal or vertical) when finding values.

conclusion.title: Great Work! 🎉
conclusion.summary: You've learned about different ways to organize and display data! Graphs and tables help us understand information quickly and spot patterns that might be hard to see in a list of numbers.
conclusion.takeaway1: Bar graphs use bars to compare amounts
conclusion.takeaway2: Pictographs use symbols to represent data
conclusion.takeaway3: Line plots show data on a number line with marks
conclusion.takeaway4: Data tables organize information in rows and columns
